notes: porter declared unbuildable after 1 attempt(s): The recursion guest's computation IS the Jolt verifier (`RV64IMACVerifier::new(...).verify()` plus `JoltVerifierPreprocessing`/`RV64IMACProof`/`JoltDevice` ark-serialize deserialization), which is only reachable through jolt-sdk's `guest-verifier` feature. That feature is defined as `guest-verifier = ["guest-std", "dep:common", "jolt-core/minimal"]`, so it unconditionally forces (a) `guest-std` = the musl/ZeroOS std runtime (`postcard/use-std`, `serde/std`, `zeroos-runtime-musl`) and (b) `jolt-core/minimal = ["ark-ec/std", "ark-ff/std", "ark-std/std", "ark-ff/asm", "rayon"]`. jolt-core is a std-only crate: `jolt-core/src` contains zero `no_std` attributes anywhere, its `minimal` feature hard-enables `std` on every arkworks crate, and it pulls `rayon` (OS threads). There is no feature path to a no_std jolt-core, so the lifted body cannot compile for riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf; the only ways to build it are switching the template to std/musl mode (forbidden — changes the study target) or re-implementing the verifier (an algorithm change). Corroborating blockers: the guest crate additionally requires jolt-sdk features `thread` (zeroos cooperative scheduler) and `random` (zeroos RNG), which guests must not have; `guest/src/lib.rs` `include!`s `./embedded_bytes.rs` and `./provable_macro.rs`, both generated at build time by the discarded host and absent from the read-only corpus tree, so the program is not self-contained; and the real input is a multi-megabyte verifier-preprocessing + proof blob (the benchmark's own host configures `max_input_size = 2_000_000` or embeds the bytes), which cannot be delivered through the frozen harness's input budget. Guest tree left untouched.
